Hi, @patrick@stwcx.xyz @paligill@gmail.com

According to https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/dbus-sensors/+/75997, I think it would also be useful to apply a similar approach in phosphor-health-monitor, so that users are notified when CPU, memory, or storage exceed their thresholds.

Do you have any suggestions on this?

New Threshold interface was proposed during the health-monitor refactor, so ideally we should be using that interface instead https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/blob/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Common/Threshold.interface.yaml.

Ignore this comment as i just realized you are using this for event interface and not threshold interface. For event interface please refer to my other comment related to using Telemetry Namespace for Metric Events.
Rather than using sensor events we should use metric related events from Redfish Telemetry namespace which are specifically for monitored metrics.

Just to confirm, do you mean I should create a new event under https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/tree/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Metric and also create a metric_event_message_registry.hpp similar to https://github.com/openbmc/bmcweb/blob/master/redfish-core/include/registries/sensor_event_message_registry.hpp ?

Ah, I see. I misunderstood your earlier comment.
Instead of creating something under xyz/openbmc_project/Metric, I should add the new event under xyz/openbmc_project/Telemetry in phosphor-dbus-interfaces, and have it associated with the telemetry_message_registry.hpp in bmcweb.

@zane.li.wiwynn@gmail.com I am referring to defining new events for metrics in metric namespace in phosphor-dbus-interfaces i.e, https://github.com/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/tree/master/yaml/xyz/openbmc_project/Metric for Redfish events in Telemtry namespace https://github.com/DMTF/Redfish-Publications/blob/main/registries/Telemetry.1.1.0.json#L1, so they can be used for Metrics.
Got it. I’ll work on defining the new events in the metric namespace

Done. CI failed because it needs:
https://gerrit.openbmc.org/c/openbmc/phosphor-dbus-interfaces/+/84216
Please use topic-based CI then to avoid issues.

Done.
By the way, I came across an interesting repo: https://github.com/openbmc/telemetry
. Do you think it would be suitable for this situation?
Please ignore my previous message. I found that  https://github.com/openbmc/telemetry only applies to /xyz/openbmc_project/sensors, not /xyz/openbmc_project/metric.

Hi @patrick@stwcx.xyz @paligill@gmail.com
Could you please help review it again when you have time?
Thank you!
Rename SEL to EventLog for better clarity.

Originally, the idea was to add a separate EventLog (SEL) option to handle event logging, while the existing Log option continued to handle journal logging. This approach gave users more flexibility to enable the functionality they needed.

The two functionalities have now been consolidated under the Log option.
Don't use common.hpp. The required fields should already be available via xyz/openbmc_project/Metric/Value/server.hpp on next line.
Done

lets create a new file health_events.hpp and health_events.cpp and move all the new code there.
Create a HealthEvent class whose singleton object can be created/initialized in HealthMonitor and then used at all places.

I’ve already created health_events.hpp and health_events.cpp.

However, the current implementation creates a HealthEvent instance for each HealthMetric rather than a singleton in HealthMonitor as suggested, because it’s inconvenient to pass it from HealthMonitor down to the lower-level HealthMetric.

If you have a better approach or suggestion, I’m happy to consider it.
Define a single API in new class generateThresholdEvent(...) by passing assert as true/false as one of the args.
Done
Why are u changing this?

Originally, there was a property assertedLog that kept track of whether each metric type/bound had been logged, so it could be resolved later. Since it was mutable, the const qualifier was removed.

Now that HealthEvent maintains this property, we can restore it as const.
Why are not extending log to eventLog and let it handle both journal logging and event logging rather than adding a new field in json?

Originally, the idea was to add a separate eventLog (sel) option to handle event logging, while the existing log option continued to handle journal logging. This approach gave users more flexibility to enable the functionality they needed.

The two functionalities have now been consolidated under the log option.
